Rex Heuermann, a former Long Island architect, pled guilty on April 8, 2026, to murdering seven women and admitted to killing an eighth, Karen Vergata, spanning from 1993 to 2010. The remains, many wrapped in burlap, were discovered along Long Island's Ocean Parkway. Heuermann, arrested in 2023, is expected to receive consecutive life sentences. Key Details of the Case The Suspect: Rex Heuermann, 62, was an architect who lived in Massapequa Park and worked in Manhattan. Guilty Plea & Victims: Heuermann admitted to killing eight women: Maureen Brainard-Barnes, Melissa Barthelemy, Megan Waterman, Amber Lynn Costello, Valerie Mack, Jessica Taylor, Sandra Costilla, and Karen Vergata. Investigation & Arrest: Heuermann was identified in 2022 through a multi-agency task force using modern DNA testing (pizza crust, hair), burner phone data, and vehicle records (a Chevrolet Avalanche). Methodology: Heuermann met the women through online advertisements, strangled them, and dumped their bodies in remote areas, including near Gilgo Beach and Manorville. Evidence: Prosecutors found that Heuermann kept detailed records, including a "blueprint" document of his crimes, and possessed over 300 guns. Victims and DiscoveriesThe investigation began with the search for Shannan Gilbert in 2010, which led to the discovery of 11 sets of remains, including the "Gilgo Four". Gilgo Four: Maureen Brainard-Barnes (found 2010), Melissa Barthelemy (2010), Megan Waterman (2010), and Amber Lynn Costello (2010). Other Victims: Valerie Mack (found 2000/2011), Jessica Taylor (2003/2011), Sandra Costilla (1993), and Karen Vergata (1996/2011). Legal Proceedings Plea Deal: Heuermann pleaded guilty to seven counts of murder and admitted to the 1996 murder of Karen Vergata, which was not initially charged. Sentencing: Sentencing is set for June 17, 2026, where he is expected to receive multiple consecutive life sentences without parole. Cooperation: As part of the plea agreement, Heuermann agreed to cooperate with the FBI. The case previously inspired the 2020 Netflix film Lost Girls.
